analysis: Examined the three units of ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift. The changed behavior (per patch excerpt and visible lines) is Autopilot-placement related: ensureModelLoaded line 207 now gates on autopilotServesModel instead of autopilotAllowsModel; unloadModel adds reconcileAutopilotPlacements() after removing the slot (head ~1146-1148); evictableModelSlots adds an autopilotHoldsModel(now:) exclusion (head ~1296-1304). These are local availability/scheduling controls within the provider process and do not touch the encryption, attestation, App Attest authorization, prefix-cache storage (T-041) or weight-hash publication paths. The visible head weight-hash code (captureWeightHash, publishWeightHash, markWeightHashUnavailable, finalizeReusableSSDLoad) is shown only as unchanged context. It fails closed on unavailable or changed hashes before SSD reuse, which is consistent with T-041 mitigations. The eviction change makes held slots non-evictable. That could reduce memory-pressure eviction, but it is a bounded availability choice; unloadModel(forEviction:) still rechecks the pinned, in-flight and reservation conditions. I could not see the implementations of autopilotServesModel, autopilotHoldsModel or reconcileAutopilotPlacements (not supplied). The remaining integration question is whether autopilotServesModel is at least as strict as autopilotAllowsModel for model-selection and authorization purposes (the 'model_not_selected' gate), and whether reconcileAutopilotPlacements, run synchronously before the awaits in unloadModel, cannot re-enter and reload the model while it is unloading. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so no definitive conclusion is possible on these. No concrete security regression is supported by the visible evidence.
